hyps.why: When the direct 0->3 edge is a parameter-free skip, edge 5 carries more of the feature learning, so upgrading it to a 3x3 conv helps more than when edge 3 is already a conv.
Replacing a weak avg_pool on edge 0 gains much more when the parallel path via edge 4 is parameter-free, so the conv is the only real feature extractor on that route.
With a weak pooling edge 0, edge 5 is a main learned path into the output, so removing it hurts far more.
With edge 0 absent, the other paths must carry the signal, so deleting edge 5 is very costly.
A strong 3x3 conv on edge 0 provides alternative capacity, so removing edge 5 costs less.
Replacing the conv on edge 5 with a skip hurts more when edge 2, the feeder into it, is only a pooling op, because little learned computation remains on that route.
With edge 4 absent, removing the direct edge 3 leaves node 3 with fewer routes for input information, causing a large drop.
With edge 0 absent, edge 1 is the only way into the graph, so a strong conv on it gives a bigger gain.
When edge 1 is already a strong conv, the extra 3x3 conv on edge 3 is redundant and gives less or negative benefit.
With edge 4 removed, the gain from adding a conv on edge 0 is small compared with when edge 4 is a skip or pool path.
